title: Solve an AI Configuration Grid
real_world_story: An AI configuration engine receives a partially filled 9 x 9 configuration grid. Each row, column, and 3 x 3 region must contain the values 1 through 9 exactly once. The system needs to complete the configuration without violating any constraint.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Backtracking with bit masks to efficiently track values already used in rows, columns, and subgrids

problem_statement: Given a partially filled 9 x 9 Sudoku grid, where empty cells are represented by 0, fill the grid so that every row, every column, and every 3 x 3 subgrid contains each number from 1 to 9 exactly once.
task: Complete the Sudoku grid and print the solved configuration.
input_format: The input contains 9 lines, each containing 9 space-separated integers. A value of 0 represents an empty cell.
output_format: Print the completed 9 x 9 Sudoku grid with each row on a separate line and values separated by spaces.
constraints: Each cell contains an integer from 0 to 9.
The given puzzle has exactly one valid solution.

examples.explanation: The completed grid satisfies all row, column, and 3 x 3 subgrid constraints.

expected_algorithm.name: Sudoku Solver
expected_algorithm.reason: Backtracking systematically fills empty cells, while bit masks can track used values efficiently in rows, columns, and 3 x 3 subgrids.

complexity.where: E is the number of empty cells.

hint: Determine which values are already used in its row, column, and 3 x 3 subgrid.
Use a bit mask to efficiently represent the available values.
Try an available value and recursively solve the remaining cells.
Backtrack when the chosen value leads to an invalid configuration.
real_world_takeaway: Constraint solving combined with bit manipulation allows AI systems to efficiently explore and validate complex configuration spaces.
